assessment.nobel_worthiness: A rare case of a clean theoretical prediction (Z2 topological order and the quantum spin Hall effect in graphene and then HgTe/CdTe) followed by a decisive experimental discovery of the edge channels. It opened an entire field of topological band theory and materials with lasting impact well beyond condensed matter. This is the kind of discovery, tied to a nameable phenomenon in nature, that I put at the centre.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall proposal. Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe quantum wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction, which is not among the credited names. A configuration of Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is defensible, but the roles of Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu and Moore (credited elsewhere or not at all) are a real allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups over about 18 years across several material systems (HgTe, 3D Bi-Sb-Te compounds via ARPES, and others). The interpretation is stable and the recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Credit overlap with the 3D topological insulator work (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore, Balents; Roy) and with the BHZ proposal that is outside the supplied credit set.
I have not independently verified the precise priority chronology of the Kane-Mele and BHZ papers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation solves the horizon and flatness problems, and the quantum-fluctuation mechanism (Mukhanov and collaborators) gives a quantitative origin for the nearly scale-invariant primordial spectrum later measured in the microwave background. It is among the most influential ideas in modern cosmology, and as a theorist in cosmology I know both its power and its weaknesses.
assessment.attribution: Guth's original proposal, Linde's new/chaotic inflation and Mukhanov's calculation of perturbations are all decisive, but Starobinsky, Sato, Albrecht, Steinhardt and Chibisov also have strong claims, so any three-person prize is contentious. The supplied three-name set is workable but not obviously fair.
assessment.maturity: The prediction of a nearly scale-invariant, adiabatic, Gaussian spectrum with a slight red tilt has been confirmed by WMAP and Planck. However, the inflationary mechanism itself remains underdetermined: primordial gravitational waves have not been seen, the model space is very large and the eternal-inflation and measure problems remain. Evidence is strong but not decisive for the specific dynamics.
uncertainties: Absence of a detected tensor signal and the multitude of viable models.
Priority disputes among Starobinsky, Guth, Linde, Albrecht, Steinhardt and Mukhanov-Chibisov.
The committee may judge the empirical status as incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theoretical prediction of magic-angle flat bands followed within about seven years by the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene. It created moire quantum materials as a new platform and is highly original, with a clear experimental signature and rapid, wide influence.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 continuum-model prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group (with Cao and collaborators) made the 2018 discovery. The credited trio maps naturally onto prediction and discovery. Yuan Cao, the lead author on the experiment, and other early contributors (e.g. Dean, Kim, Young, Yacoby, Efetov, Lau) could raise allocation questions.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many independent groups across twisted multilayers and TMDs, with fractional Chern insulators now following. Interpretation of the superconductivity and the correlated states is still in flux, but the existence of the phenomena is very well established. Timing is plausible but the field is still young.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism in the superconducting phase is not settled.
Whether a younger field should be recognized now or later.
Allocation of credit to the early experimental team members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and the evidence for sources (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, the Galactic plane), opened neutrino astronomy. It is a true discovery in nature about cosmic-ray accelerators, and it needed a remarkable instrument in Antarctic ice.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit is a single name. Halzen was the intellectual driver and long-time spokesperson, but IceCube is a large collaboration and a prize for one person is hard to defend alone. Others who built the detector (e.g. leadership of AMANDA/IceCube and DOE/NSF-supported teams) are not in the credited set, so the supplied credit can only support a narrow configuration.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established, with independent confirmation from ANTARES/Baikal and from different analyses. Source identification is now at the 4 to 5 sigma level for a few objects. This is a mature discovery but the source population is still being worked out.
uncertainties: Attribution to one individual of a large-collaboration result.
The source associations are not yet at a very high significance for most classes of objects.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a surprisingly large theta-13 by Daya Bay (and RENO, with Double Chooz) made CP violation in the lepton sector experimentally accessible and shaped the whole neutrino programme (DUNE, Hyper-Kamiokande, JUNO). It is a decisive and unambiguous measurement of a fundamental parameter.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang as spokesperson, Luk as co-spokesperson) and RENO (Kim) announced essentially simultaneously in 2012. The Double Chooz team (Cabrera, Lasserre and others) is not credited, and earlier proposals by Hanyang and Daya Bay colleagues, and the T2K electron-appearance indication, complicate priority. The three-name set is plausible but leaves out a competing group.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent experiments confirmed the result and the precision now reaches a few percent. The result is very stable, though it is only 14 years old and neutrino oscillations were recognized in 2015, so the committee might see this as a follow-on.
uncertainties: Fairness of leaving out Double Chooz and T2K.
Whether the committee sees a precision parameter measurement as being at the level of the oscillation discovery already honoured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's proposal of magic-wavelength lattice trapping and its realization with Ye's strontium clocks produced time standards at the 10^-18 level, far beyond the caesium standard. The impact on metrology, tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and potentially dark-matter searches is large and ongoing.
assessment.attribution: Katori invented the optical lattice clock concept and Ye brought it to extreme precision. The two-name configuration is clean, although Ye also appears on the ultracold molecule candidate and Hall, Hansch (already laureates) and the Yb and Al+ clock groups could be raised.
assessment.maturity: Several independent labs now operate lattice clocks, and international comparisons validate the accuracy. The redefinition of the second is under discussion. This is mature, though it is an invention and its fundamental-physics payoff is still developing.
uncertainties: Whether lattice clocks versus trapped-ion clocks deserve separate recognition.
Overlap with prior frequency-comb and laser cooling prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BAO provide a robust standard ruler: predicted by Peebles-Yu and Sunyaev-Zeldovich as acoustic features in the matter distribution and detected in 2005 in SDSS and 2dFGRS. They now underpin dark-energy constraints, including recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy. A cosmologically central discovery with direct implications for the nature of dark energy.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein led the SDSS detection and Cole and Percival the 2dFGRS detection, while Sunyaev (with Zeldovich, deceased) and Peebles and Yu (Peebles already a laureate) did the theory. The supplied names include four, so a three-person configuration requires choosing between Cole and Percival. The prediction credit is a real allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by multiple surveys (BOSS, eBOSS, DESI). The measurement is very robust; its cosmological interpretation, however, is currently entangled with the Hubble tension and recent hints of time-varying dark energy.
uncertainties: Unresolved credit between the 2dFGRS and SDSS teams and the theorists.
Possible reinterpretation if dark-energy evolution is established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1977 Leinaas-Myrheim demonstration that identical particles in two dimensions can have fractional exchange statistics, and Wilczek's 1982 anyons, introduced a conceptual extension of quantum statistics that underpins fractional quantum Hall physics and topological quantum computation. This is a deep conceptual discovery of lasting importance.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim's configuration-space argument predated Wilczek, and Wilczek named and developed anyons. Halperin and Arovas-Schrieffer-Wilczek tied the idea to the quantum Hall effect. The credited set is cleanly theoretical, but experimental confirmation belongs to different people (Fève, Manfra, Bartolomei and others), so a theory-only prize may be seen as incomplete.
assessment.maturity: The 2020 interferometry and collision experiments give direct evidence for fractional statistics in the quantum Hall regime, and non-Abelian anyon evidence is still pending. Recognition of the foundational theory is timely, but one might wait for non-Abelian confirmation.
uncertainties: Whether the experimental demonstrations should be recognized jointly.
Wilczek is already a laureate, which may affect how the committee views a second prize.
